entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_delete_draft
entries.description: Move a draft in the signed-in user's Outlook mailbox to Deleted Items (recoverable). Refuses to act on a message that is not a draft. Returns success if the draft is already gone. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

messageId.description: The id of the draft message to delete (as returned by outlook_create_draft).

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_delete_event
entries.description: Delete a calendar event from the signed-in user's own calendar. If the user is the organizer, a cancellation email is sent to any attendees (with the optional comment); if the user is an attendee, the event is removed from their own calendar only. The event moves to Deleted Items (recoverable), but the cancellation email cannot be unsent. Returns success if the event is not in the user's calendar (including already gone). Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

eventId.description: The id of the event to delete (as returned by outlook_create_event or outlook_calendar_search). For recurring events, pass the series-master id to cancel the whole series, or an individual occurrence id to cancel one occurrence.

comment.description: Optional plain-text note included in the cancellation email to attendees. Only used when the signed-in user is the organizer.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_email_search
entries.description: Search Outlook mail by text, sender, recipient, date, folder or shared mailbox. Read full emails with the read_resource tool on the returned URIs. Filters combine with AND, except three combinations that are rejected. When a request would need one, drop a parameter instead of sending it. (1) `order: "oldest"` with `query` or `recipient`. For the earliest, drop `order` and compare dates across all pages. `order: "newest"` with either is accepted but not applied: for the latest emails about a topic send `query` (add `afterDateTime` only if the user gave a time window; never invent an old date) and sort the returned dates yourself, checking later pages. (2) With `folderName`: a date (`afterDateTime`/`beforeDateTime`) together with `query` or `recipient`. In the user's own mailbox, omit `folderName`, search all folders, and tell the user you did. (3) With `mailboxOwnerEmail`: any `recipient`, or `query` together with `sender` or a date. Keep `mailboxOwnerEmail` (and any `folderName`), drop `recipient` and `query`, send any `sender`/date filters, and check the returned subjects and recipients; retry with `query` alone (no `sender` or dates) only if nothing useful comes back. For 'emails I sent to X' or 'the last thing I emailed X', send `recipient` with no `folderName` or `order`, keep hits whose `sender` is the user or starts with `/O=`, pick the newest, and narrow with `afterDateTime` if the page is full. Send at least one of `query`, `sender`, `recipient`, a date, `folderName`, `mailboxOwnerEmail` or `order`; for the newest Inbox emails, send `order: "newest"` alone. If the response includes a final item with `nextOffset`, there are more results — pass that value as the `offset` parameter to fetch the next page. Always start with offset: 0. When a reliable total is available, that item also includes `totalResultCount` (the number of results across all pages). If the final item includes `nextCursor` instead of `nextOffset`, pass that value as the `cursor` parameter (and omit `offset`). Always start with no cursor.

query.description: Text to search for in email subject, body, or attachments. Omit it, or send '*', to search by the other parameters only. The text must have balanced ( ) and an even number of " — wrap a phrase in double quotes (e.g. '"thanks :)"') to search literal parentheses — unless it is sent with `folderName` or `mailboxOwnerEmail` and no `sender` or `recipient`; then it is not checked and its double quotes are removed. Refused with `order: "oldest"` (leave out `order`), with a date when `folderName` or `mailboxOwnerEmail` is set, and with `sender` when `mailboxOwnerEmail` is set; then leave out `query` in a shared mailbox, `folderName` in the user's own.

folderName.description: Name of a specific Outlook mail folder to search in (case-insensitive). Common folders 'Inbox', 'Sent Items', 'Drafts', 'Deleted Items', 'Archive', 'Junk Email', 'Outbox' are recognized directly (locale-independent; works for delegated mailboxes). Any other name is looked up by enumerating the mailbox's folders. Use ONLY when the user explicitly names a mail folder. Do NOT use this to filter by a person's name — use 'sender' or 'recipient' instead. Omit to search all folders (with `order`, see its Inbox default). With it, a date (`afterDateTime`/`beforeDateTime`) is refused if `query` or `recipient` is also sent: in the user's own mailbox, leave out `folderName` then.

mailboxOwnerEmail.description: Email address of a shared mailbox or another user's mailbox you have delegated access to. Omit to search your own mailbox. Requires Mail.Read.Shared permission. Refused with any `recipient`, and with `query` plus `sender` or a date: keep this and leave out `recipient`, and `query` when a `sender` or date is sent.

sender.description: Sender to filter by: an email address, a domain, or a full display name. With `folderName`, `mailboxOwnerEmail` or `order` and no `query` or `recipient`, it matches any part of the sender's email address and never a display name. Otherwise it goes to the search index, where a full address or the full display name is the safest form and a fragment such as the first letters of an address may not match. A full address can miss some mail from someone in the user's own organization. If results from the user's own mailbox look incomplete, also try the display name without `folderName` and `order`; in a shared mailbox only the address form works. With `mailboxOwnerEmail`, it is refused together with `query`: leave out `query`.

recipient.description: Email address of a recipient to filter by. Matches TO, CC, or BCC recipients. Without `folderName` it searches every folder, including Sent Items. Refused with `mailboxOwnerEmail` (leave out `recipient`), with `order: "oldest"` (leave out `order`), and with a date when `folderName` is set (leave out `folderName`).

afterDateTime.description: Return emails received after this date/time. Accepts natural language: 'yesterday', 'last week', 'March 15 2024', ISO dates, etc. With `folderName` or `mailboxOwnerEmail`, it is refused together with `query` or `recipient`: keep the date and leave out `folderName` (own mailbox) or `query`/`recipient` (shared mailbox).

beforeDateTime.description: Return emails received before this date/time. Accepts natural language: 'today', 'next month', ISO dates, etc. With `folderName` or `mailboxOwnerEmail`, it is refused together with `query` or `recipient`: keep the date and leave out `folderName` (own mailbox) or `query`/`recipient` (shared mailbox).

order.description: Sort results by received date: 'newest' (most recent first) or 'oldest' (earliest first). Without `query` or `recipient`, it sorts the Inbox unless `folderName` names another folder (e.g. 'Sent Items'); with them, see the tool description. When omitted, a `folderName` or `mailboxOwnerEmail` search without `query` or `recipient` returns newest first; other searches are not guaranteed to be in date order. `"oldest"` is refused with `query` or `recipient`: leave out `order` then.

offset.description: Number of results to skip; see the paging note in the tool description. Default: 0. Ignored when `cursor` is set, and ignored by searches in a folder or shared mailbox that include `query` or `recipient`, which page by `cursor`.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned in a prior response as `nextCursor`. Pass it back unchanged to fetch the next page; other parameters, including `limit`, are ignored when set.

limit.description: Maximum number of emails to return. Default: 10, Max: 25

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_find_available_time
entries.description: Find open time slots for a meeting between the signed-in user and the given participants. Searches the given UTC date range and returns up to maxCandidates slots ranked by confidence. Each returned slot's start and end are {dateTime, timeZone} objects in exactly the shape event creation accepts, so if outlook_create_event is available a chosen slot can be passed straight to it. Inputs are UTC. Each output slot's dateTime is a wall-clock time in the paired timeZone (the user's Outlook mailbox zone, or UTC when that is unavailable); present dateTime together with its timeZone and do not apply a further UTC-to-local conversion unless the user is known to be in a different zone. The result's nowDateTime is the authoritative current time; if it differs materially from Claude's assumed 'now', re-issue the search with corrected dates before interpreting relative references like 'tomorrow'. Suggestions are NOT confined to working hours (activityDomain is unrestricted, not the Graph default of 'work'), so filter out-of-hours slots yourself if appropriate. If Graph could not read some participants' calendars, those emails are listed in unavailableParticipants and marked 'unknown' in each slot's attendeeAvailability; treat their availability as unconfirmed.

participants.description: Participant email addresses (max 50). The signed-in user is always included as organizer. Omit or pass an empty list to search the organizer's own availability.

afterDateTime.description: Start of the search range (ISO 8601 UTC: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ)

beforeDateTime.description: End of the search range (ISO 8601 UTC: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ)

maxCandidates.description: Maximum number of time slots to return

isOrganizerOptional.description: Whether the organizer (signed-in user) attendance is optional

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_forward_mail
entries.description: Forward an existing message from the signed-in user's Outlook mailbox to the given recipients, with an optional plain-text note prepended. The original message body is forwarded immediately and a copy is saved to Sent Items. Messages with attachments cannot be forwarded. Recipients are capped at 50. The forwarded message is stamped with the X-AI-Generated attribution header. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

messageId.description: The id of the message to forward (as returned by outlook_email_search or the read resource tool).

to.description: Recipient email addresses to forward the message to

comment.description: Optional plain-text note prepended above the forwarded message.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_modify_labels
entries.description: Add/remove labels (Outlook categories) on a single message, and/or move it to a folder. Categories are read-modify-written so tags applied in Outlook are never clobbered. Trash-family move destinations are rejected — this tool files, it does not delete. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

messageId.description: The id of the message to relabel.

addCategories.description: Category names to add (by displayName; case-insensitive, existing tags are not duplicated).

removeCategories.description: Category names to remove (case-insensitive; names not on the message are reported, not errors).

moveToFolderId.description: Optionally move the message to this folder (when the 'label' is a folder). Trash-family destinations are rejected — this tool files, it does not delete.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_modify_thread_labels
entries.description: Add/remove labels (Outlook categories) across every message of a conversation, and/or move the whole thread to a folder. Categories are read-modify-written per message; category and move outcomes are reported per message and independently (a move can fail where the relabel succeeded). Trash-family destinations are rejected — this tool files, it does not delete. Thread members sitting anywhere under Deleted Items or Junk are NOT moved (filing must not un-delete or un-spam them) — they are counted and named in the result, and categories still apply to them. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

conversationId.description: The conversation id of the thread to relabel (read a message with the read resource tool — its metadata includes conversationId).

addCategories.description: Category names to add to every message of the thread.

removeCategories.description: Category names to remove from every message of the thread.

moveToFolderId.description: Optionally move every message of the thread to this folder. Trash-family destinations are rejected — this tool files, it does not delete.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_respond_to_event
entries.description: Respond to a meeting invitation as the signed-in user: accept, decline, or tentatively accept. Optionally include a comment or propose a new time (decline/tentative only). By default a response email is sent to the organizer; set sendResponse to false to update the calendar silently. Declining removes the event from the calendar. Only valid on events where the user is an attendee (organizers cannot respond to their own meeting). Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

eventId.description: The id of the meeting invitation to respond to (as returned by outlook_calendar_search).

response.description: The response to send. Declining removes the event from the calendar.

comment.description: Optional plain-text note included in the response email to the organizer. Requires sendResponse to be true.

sendResponse.description: Whether to send a response email to the organizer. If false, the calendar is updated silently.

timeZone.description: Time zone name. Accepts Windows time-zone names (e.g. 'Pacific Standard Time') or common IANA names (e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'); IANA names are mapped to Windows names before sending.
Time zone name. Accepts Windows time-zone names (e.g. 'Pacific Standard Time') or common IANA names (e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'); IANA names are mapped to Windows names before sending.

proposedNewTime.description: Propose a new time (only valid with response 'decline' or 'tentative' and when sendResponse is true).

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_send_draft
entries.description: Send an existing draft from the signed-in user's Outlook mailbox by the message id returned from outlook_create_draft. Before sending, the draft is re-validated against outlook_send_mail's limits (at least one recipient across To/Cc/Bcc; total recipients ≤ 50; subject ≤ 255 chars; body within a coarse size bound of 2500000 chars; no attachments; From/Sender/Reply-To not set to a different identity than the signed-in user; no content Exchange's SafeHTML filter removes). The draft is never modified. The sent message is saved to Sent Items. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

messageId.description: The id of the draft message to send, as returned by outlook_create_draft.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_send_mail
entries.description: Send an email from the signed-in user's Outlook mailbox. The message is saved to Sent Items. HTML bodies are sanitized before sending. Total recipients across to/cc/bcc is capped at 50. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

body.description:
Email body. For any message with paragraphs, lists, or links, pass HTML (each paragraph in

...

, line breaks as
) and set bodyType to 'html' so the formatting is preserved in Outlook. Max 500,000 characters.

bodyType.description: Body content type. Use 'html' for any message that has paragraphs, lists, links, or emphasis. 'html' is sanitized against a narrow allowlist (headings, paragraphs, links, lists, basic formatting, tables, pre) before sending; tags outside the allowlist, including ,

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_trash_thread
entries.description: Move every message of a conversation (email thread) to Deleted Items. This is a recoverable soft delete — messages stay in Deleted Items until retention empties it, and the result records each message's previous folder so the thread can be restored. Refuses threads larger than 100 messages. Messages already directly in Deleted Items are left untouched. Acts on the signed-in user's own mailbox (/me) ONLY: a conversationId read from a shared or delegated mailbox (a resource URI with an ?owner= suffix) will NOT trash the shared mailbox's thread — it may instead move the user's own copies of that thread. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

conversationId.description: The conversation id of the thread to move to Deleted Items (read a message with the read resource tool — its metadata includes conversationId; outlook_email_search results do not). Must come from the signed-in user's OWN mailbox: an id read from a shared or delegated mailbox (an ?owner= resource URI) will not trash the shared mailbox's thread — it may instead move the user's own copies of it.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_untrash_thread
entries.description: Restore a previously trashed conversation (email thread) from Deleted Items. With the restoreMap from the outlook_trash_thread result, each message goes back to its original folder; without it, everything goes to Inbox (Outlook does not record a message's pre-deletion folder). Messages of the thread not currently in Deleted Items are skipped. Refuses oversized work loudly: more than 100 in-trash members without a restoreMap, or a conversation with more than 1000 total mailbox messages, is rejected before anything moves. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

conversationId.description: The conversation id of the thread to restore from Deleted Items (from the outlook_trash_thread result, or read a message with the read resource tool).

messageId.description: The message's CURRENT id in Deleted Items — the `newId` from the outlook_trash_thread result.

destinationFolderId.description: The folder to restore this message to — the `previousParentFolderId` from the outlook_trash_thread result.

restoreMap.description: Per-message restore destinations, as recorded by outlook_trash_thread (moved[]: newId → messageId, previousParentFolderId → destinationFolderId). When a map is supplied, ONLY mapped messages are restored — in-trash messages without an entry are left there (either not moved by the trash call — already in Deleted Items — or deliberately not mapped for this restore). Omit the map entirely to restore every in-trash conversation message to Inbox (Outlook does not record a message's pre-deletion folder, so original-folder restore only works with this mapping).

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_update_draft
entries.description: Update an existing draft in the signed-in user's Outlook mailbox by its message id. Only the supplied fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. Refuses to modify a message that is not a draft. HTML bodies containing anything outside the outbound allowlist are rejected (not silently rewritten). Total recipients across supplied to/cc/bcc is capped at 50. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

messageId.description: The id of the draft message to update (as returned by outlook_create_draft).

to.description: Replace the To recipients. Omit to leave unchanged; pass an empty array to clear.

cc.description: Replace the CC recipients. Omit to leave unchanged; pass an empty array to clear.

bcc.description: Replace the BCC recipients. Omit to leave unchanged; pass an empty array to clear.

subject.description: Replace the subject. Omit to leave unchanged.

body.description:
Replace the body content. For any message with paragraphs, lists, or links, pass HTML (each paragraph in

...

, line breaks as
) and set bodyType to 'html' so the formatting is preserved in Outlook. Omit to leave unchanged. On a reply or forward draft this replaces the entire body including the quoted original; to add reply content above the quote, pass body to outlook_create_reply_draft or outlook_create_reply_all_draft instead.

bodyType.description: Body content type. Use 'html' for any message that has paragraphs, lists, links, or emphasis. Required when body is supplied; rejected when body is omitted (no default — an implicit 'text' would silently convert an HTML draft to plain text). 'html' must use only the allowlist (headings, paragraphs, links, lists, b/i/strong/em/strike, code, tables, br/hr, div, pre); bodies containing anything else — scripts, iframes, event handlers, images, span/font/blockquote, comments or other <!...>/<?...?> markup — are rejected, not stripped.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__outlook_update_event
entries.description: Update an existing calendar event by its id. Only the supplied fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. WARNING: supplying 'attendees' REPLACES the entire attendee list — attendees omitted from the new list are removed and receive a cancellation. Attendees receive update notifications automatically. HTML bodies are sanitized. Attendee count is capped at 50. If the signed-in user is not the organizer, only their own copy of the event is updated (changes may not propagate to other attendees) and a warning is included in the result. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

eventId.description: The id of the event to update (as returned by outlook_create_event or outlook_calendar_search). For recurring events, pass the series-master id to change the whole series, or an individual occurrence id (from /instances) to change one occurrence.

subject.description: Replace the subject. Omit to leave unchanged.

timeZone.description: Time zone name. Accepts Windows time-zone names (e.g. 'Pacific Standard Time') or common IANA names (e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'); IANA names are mapped to Windows names before sending.

start.description: Replace the start. Omit to leave unchanged.

timeZone.description: Time zone name. Accepts Windows time-zone names (e.g. 'Pacific Standard Time') or common IANA names (e.g. 'America/Los_Angeles'); IANA names are mapped to Windows names before sending.

end.description: Replace the end. Omit to leave unchanged.

body.description: Replace the body content. Omit to leave unchanged.

bodyType.description: Body content type when body is supplied. Required whenever body is supplied so an existing HTML event is not silently downgraded to plain text. 'html' is sanitized before saving.

attendees.description: Replace the ENTIRE attendee list. Graph's PATCH on attendees replaces the whole collection — anyone not listed here is removed and receives a cancellation. Omit to leave attendees unchanged.

location.description: Replace the location display name. Omit to leave unchanged.

isOnlineMeeting.description: Add a Teams meeting. Once added, Graph does not allow removing it, so only 'true' is accepted here.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__read_resource
entries.description: Read full content of any Microsoft Graph resource by URI. Use this tool after search tools return URIs. Returns complete resource data including: email bodies, file contents, calendar event details, folder listings, chat messages, etc. Each resource type returns different fields based on what's available.

uri.description: The URI of the resource to read. Supported formats:        'file:///{driveId}/{itemId}' or 'file:///{driveId}/{folder path}/{file name}' (SharePoint/OneDrive files; the path is relative to the drive root — when adapting a SharePoint web URL, omit the document-library segment such as "Shared Documents"; web URLs (https://) are NOT supported),        'site:///{siteId}/{groupId}' (SharePoint sites),        'mail:///messages/{messageId}[?owner={email}]' (Outlook emails; owner for shared/delegated mailboxes),        'mail:///folders/{folderId}' (Outlook folders),        'calendar:///events/{eventId}[?owner={email}]' (Calendar events; owner for delegated calendars),        'page:///sites/{siteId}/pages/{pageId}' (SharePoint pages),        'drive:///{entityType}/{entityId}' (OneDrive drives; entityType must be one of: users, groups, sites. Use entityType=users with entityId=me for the signed-in user's drives),        'meeting-transcript:///events/{joinUrlToken}[?start={iso}&end={iso}]' (Teams meeting transcripts — pass the meetingTranscriptUrl field from a calendar event read verbatim; the token is an opaque base64url encoding of the join URL; start/end scope a recurring series to one occurrence, omit to receive the most recent transcripts of the series (capped)),        'teams:///chats/{chatId}/messages/{messageId}' (Teams chat messages),        'teams:///teams/{teamId}/channels/{channelId}/messages/{messageId}' (Teams channel messages)

startPage.description: For paginated file:/// (SharePoint/OneDrive) reads only: 1-based page number to start from. Applies to PDFs and Office formats that the connector reads via Graph's PDF conversion (e.g. docx, pptx), where a page is a document page; to .xlsx workbooks, where a page is a worksheet, numbered as in the list at the top of the text (hidden sheets count; if the text instead begins by saying the workbook was read through its PDF conversion, a page is a PDF page); and to plain-text files (.txt, .csv, .tsv, .json, .md, .xml, .html, .htm, .log), where a page is as many whole lines as fit in one call and each call returns one page (for .csv/.tsv a line is a record — a line break inside a double-quoted field does not end it — and the header line is repeated on every page after the first). When more remains, the text ends with a footer like '[truncated: pages 1-14 of 16 — re-call with startPage=15]', '[Sheets 3–20 were not read; call again with startPage=3 to continue from sheet 3 ("Budget").]' or '[page 1 — lines 1–590 of a 6800000-byte file — more follows; re-call with startPage=2]'; follow that hint to read later pages. A plain-text file returned with no footer is complete; otherwise its final page ends in 'last page'. Applies also to a folder listing, where a page is 200 entries and each call returns one page; a final 'Note:' line says when to re-call with the next startPage. Each call can return up to ~200k characters of text, so many pages may fill the context window quickly. Ignored for every other URI scheme and for image reads.

endPage.description: 1-based last page to extract, inclusive (for .xlsx workbooks, the last worksheet). Must be >= startPage. Same applicability as startPage; plain-text reads and folder listings return one page per call, so it has no effect on them.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__search_people
entries.description: Search for people by name or email address. Results are drawn from and relevance-ranked by the signed-in user's own communication and collaboration history (mail, Teams, directory), so frequent contacts rank highest. Use this to resolve a name to an id or userPrincipalName before calling teams_create_chat (when that write-gated tool is available), or to find an email address before composing a message. Returns id, displayName, userPrincipalName, mail, jobTitle, relevanceScore, and personType (class/subclass, e.g. Person/OrganizationUser). Only Person/OrganizationUser entries (directory users with a non-null userPrincipalName) are valid teams_create_chat members when that tool is enabled; Person/PersonalContact entries are Outlook contacts reachable by mail instead.

query.description: Name, email address, or other identifying text to search for. Matches against names and email addresses of people relevant to the signed-in user.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default 10, max 25).

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__sharepoint_copy_item
entries.description: Copy a SharePoint or OneDrive file or folder to another folder, including across drives and sites. Graph runs the copy asynchronously; this tool polls the operation for up to 45 seconds. If the copy completes in time, returns the new item's id and resource URI; if it is still running (large folders can take longer), the tool returns an isError result containing the monitor URL — the copy continues server-side, so poll the monitor URL for completion rather than retrying this call. Fails if the destination already contains an item with the target name (the source name, or newName when supplied); resolve with a different newName. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

driveId.description: The Graph driveId containing the source item (from a file:/// resource URI or sharepoint_search / sharepoint_folder_search results).

itemId.description: The item id of the file or folder to copy.

destinationDriveId.description: The driveId of the destination drive. Omit to copy within the source drive.

destinationParentItemId.description: The item id of the destination folder. Use 'root' for the drive root.

newName.description: Optional new name for the copy. Omit to keep the source name. The copy fails on any destination name collision (source name or newName); resolve with a different newName.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__sharepoint_create_folder
entries.description: Create a new folder in a SharePoint document library or OneDrive folder. By default fails if an item with the same name already exists; pass conflictBehavior 'rename' to let Graph pick a unique name. Returns the created folder's id, webUrl, and a file:/// resource URI readable via read_resource. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

driveId.description: The Graph driveId of the SharePoint document library or OneDrive drive to create the folder in (from sharepoint_search / sharepoint_folder_search results or a file:/// resource URI).

parentItemId.description: The item id of the parent folder. Omit for the drive root, or pass a folder's item id from sharepoint_folder_search.

name.description: Name for the new folder. Must not contain path separators — create nested folders with one call per level.

conflictBehavior.description: What to do if an item with this name already exists in the parent: 'fail' (default — return an error) or 'rename' (Graph picks a unique name).

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__sharepoint_delete_item
entries.description: Delete a SharePoint or OneDrive file or folder by its driveId and item id. The item moves to the drive's recycle bin and is recoverable there for up to 93 days (site-collection admins can restore beyond the first-stage bin). Deleting a folder also deletes its contents. Returns success if the item is already gone. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

driveId.description: The Graph driveId containing the item (from a file:/// resource URI or sharepoint_search / sharepoint_folder_search results).

itemId.description: The item id of the file or folder to delete. Deleting a folder also deletes its contents.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__sharepoint_folder_search
entries.description: Search SharePoint folders by name (partial match supported). Returns folder metadata and URIs - use read_resource tool with returned URIs to list folder contents. Case-insensitive search. Returns max 50 folders per request. If the response includes a final item with `nextOffset`, there are more results — pass that value as the `offset` parameter to fetch the next page. Always start with offset: 0. When a reliable total is available, that item also includes `totalResultCount` (the number of results across all pages).

name.description: Name or partial name of the folder to search for. Case-insensitive partial matching supported

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination. Start at 0 and pass the `nextOffset` value from the prior response to fetch the next page. Default: 0

limit.description: Maximum number of folders to return. Default: 10, Max: 50

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__sharepoint_move_item
entries.description: Move a SharePoint or OneDrive file or folder to a different parent folder within the same drive (optionally renaming it). The item id is preserved; its webUrl and path change. Graph does not support moving across drives with this operation — to relocate across drives or sites, use sharepoint_copy_item, verify it returned a completed (non-error) result, then sharepoint_delete_item. Fails if the destination already has an item with the same name. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

driveId.description: The Graph driveId containing the item to move (from a file:/// resource URI or sharepoint_search / sharepoint_folder_search results).

Fails if a sibling already uses the new name. Use sharepoint_move_item to change the parent folder. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

driveId.description: The Graph driveId containing the item (from a file:/// resource URI or sharepoint_search / sharepoint_folder_search results).

itemId.description: The item id of the file or folder to rename.

newName.description: The new name for the item, including extension for files. Must not contain path separators — use sharepoint_move_item to change the parent folder.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__sharepoint_search
entries.description: Search SharePoint documents and pages by content, filename, or metadata. Returns document metadata - use read_resource tool with returned URIs for full content. Filters use AND logic (must match ALL criteria). Use sharepoint_folder_search tool to find folders. Returns max 50 documents per request. If the response includes a final item with `nextOffset`, there are more results — pass that value as the `offset` parameter to fetch the next page. Always start with offset: 0. query.description: Text to search for in document content, filename, or metadata. Required field

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination. Start at 0 and pass the `nextOffset` value from the prior response to fetch the next page. Default: 0

limit.description: Maximum number of documents to return. Default: 10, Max: 50

fileType.description: Filter by file extension (e.g., 'pdf', 'docx', 'xlsx'). Omit to search all file types

folderName.description: Filter by folder name. Searches within folders matching this name (partial match supported)

author.description: Filter by document author name or email (partial match supported)

afterDateTime.description: Return documents modified after this date/time. Accepts natural language: 'yesterday', 'last week', 'March 15 2024', ISO dates, etc.

beforeDateTime.description: Return documents modified before this date/time. Accepts natural language: 'today', 'next month', ISO dates, etc.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__sharepoint_update_file
entries.description: Replace the content of an existing SharePoint or OneDrive file by its driveId and item id (content up to 1048576 bytes). Refuses to act on a folder. The prior content is overwritten; libraries with versioning enabled keep the previous version in history. For text, prefer 'content'; contentBase64 must be strict unbroken base64 (no whitespace or data-URI prefix). Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

driveId.description: The Graph driveId containing the file (from a search result or the first path segment of a file:/// resource URI).

itemId.description: The item id of the existing file to overwrite (from a search result or the second path segment of a file:/// resource URI).

content.description: Replacement file content (the prior content is replaced in full; Graph keeps version history where the library has versioning enabled) as UTF-8 text. Prefer this for any text payload (plain text, JSON, Markdown, source code); use contentBase64 only for binary data. Exactly one of content / contentBase64 must be supplied. Byte size must not exceed 1048576. For Office, PDF, and MP4 extensions (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.doc/.pdf/.mp4, ...) the bytes MUST be a complete file of that format (binary formats via contentBase64); plain text under such a name is refused.

contentBase64.description: Replacement file content (the prior content is replaced in full; Graph keeps version history where the library has versioning enabled), base64-encoded. Use this only for binary payloads; for text, pass 'content' instead. For Office, PDF, and MP4 extensions (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.doc/.pdf/.mp4, ...) the bytes MUST be a complete file of that format (binary formats via contentBase64); plain text under such a name is refused. Exactly one of content / contentBase64 must be supplied. Decoded size must not exceed 1048576 bytes. Must be strict standard base64: one unbroken string (A–Z a–z 0–9 + /, '=' padding only at the end), with no whitespace, line wrapping, or data-URI prefix. If it is rejected, generate the base64 again and send it unmodified; do not split a single binary file across calls — there is no chunked upload.

expectedBytes.description: The exact size in bytes of the source file (decoded byte length, not the base64 character count). Supply this only when you have the byte count first-hand from where the file was produced — for example, computed in the same code-execution run that built the bytes. Omit it otherwise; a guessed or approximate value will reject a valid upload. When supplied and the received content decodes to a different length, the write is refused.

Returns the created item's id, webUrl, and a file:/// resource URI readable via read_resource. For text, prefer 'content'; contentBase64 must be strict unbroken base64 (no whitespace or data-URI prefix). content.description: File content as UTF-8 text. Prefer this for any text payload (plain text, JSON, Markdown, source code); use contentBase64 only for binary data. Exactly one of content / contentBase64 must be supplied. Byte size must not exceed 1048576. For Office, PDF, and MP4 extensions (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.doc/.pdf/.mp4, ...) the bytes MUST be a complete file of that format (binary formats via contentBase64); plain text under such a name is refused.

contentBase64.description: File content, base64-encoded. Use this only for binary payloads; for text, pass 'content' instead. For Office, PDF, and MP4 extensions (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.doc/.pdf/.mp4, ...) the bytes MUST be a complete file of that format (binary formats via contentBase64); plain text under such a name is refused. Exactly one of content / contentBase64 must be supplied. Decoded size must not exceed 1048576 bytes. Must be strict standard base64: one unbroken string (A–Z a–z 0–9 + /, '=' padding only at the end), with no whitespace, line wrapping, or data-URI prefix. If it is rejected, generate the base64 again and send it unmodified; do not split a single binary file across calls — there is no chunked upload.

expectedBytes.description: The exact size in bytes of the source file (decoded byte length, not the base64 character count). Supply this only when you have the byte count first-hand from where the file was produced — for example, computed in the same code-execution run that built the bytes. Omit it otherwise; a guessed or approximate value will reject a valid upload. When supplied and the received content decodes to a different length, the write is refused.

conflictBehavior.description: What to do if a file with this name already exists in the parent folder: 'fail' (default — return an error), 'replace' (overwrite — destructive), or 'rename' (Graph picks a unique name like 'file 1.txt').

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__teams_create_chat
entries.description: Create a Teams chat (1:1 or group) with the given members as the signed-in user. The signed-in user is added as a member automatically. For chatType oneOnOne this is find-or-create: if a 1:1 chat between the two users already exists Graph returns it instead of creating a new one. For chatType group a new chat is always created (at most 50 members per call). Returns the chat id (pass to teams_send_chat_message to post) and webUrl. Creating a chat does not send a message. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

members.description: AAD user object ids (GUID) or userPrincipalNames (UPN, usually email-shaped) of the chat members. The signed-in user is added automatically if not listed. For chatType oneOnOne supply exactly one other user; for group supply two or more (at most 50).

chatType.description: oneOnOne: a 1:1 chat with one other member (find-or-create: if a 1:1 chat between the two users already exists Graph returns it instead of creating a new one). group: a group chat with two or more other members (always creates a new chat).

topic.description: Display name for the chat. Only valid for chatType group; omit for oneOnOne.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__teams_list_channel_messages
entries.description: List the messages in a Microsoft Teams channel the signed-in user is a member of: by default the channel's top-level messages (conversation roots), or, when parentMessageId is set, the replies in that conversation. Each item carries the message id, sender, timestamps, webUrl, attachments (names and links only), and a sanitized body preview of up to 1000 characters; top-level items also carry a teams:/// uri for read_resource, which returns the full body, mentions, and reactions. Top-level messages come in Graph's order, by last activity in each conversation; use createdDateTime to order replies. System event messages (member added, channel renamed, ...) have a null from and bodyPreview and a messageType other than 'message'. Use a top-level id as the messageId for teams_reply_channel_message when that write-gated tool is available. If the response includes a final item with `nextCursor`, there are more results; pass that value as the `cursor` parameter (keeping the other parameters the same) to fetch the next page. Always start with no cursor.

teamId.description: The id (group id GUID) of the team that owns the channel. Obtain from teams_list_teams, or from the teamId segment embedded in the channelUri on chat_message_search channel results (percent-decode it first).

channelId.description: The id of the channel, typically of the form 19:...@thread.tacv2. Obtain from teams_list_channels.

parentMessageId.description: Omit to list the channel's top-level messages (conversation roots). Set to a top-level message id to list the replies in that conversation instead.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned in a prior response as `nextCursor`. Pass it back unchanged, with the same teamId, channelId, and parentMessageId, to fetch the next page; `limit` is ignored when `cursor` is set. Omit on the first call.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Default: 20, max: 50.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__teams_list_channels
entries.description: List the channels in a team the signed-in user is a member of. Returns each channel's id, displayName, description, membershipType, and webUrl. Use the id with teams_list_channel_messages (when available) to read the channel, or with teams_send_channel_message / teams_reply_channel_message when those write-gated tools are available.

teamId.description: The id of the team whose channels to list. Obtain from teams_list_teams, or from the teamId segment embedded in the channelUri on chat_message_search channel results (percent-decode it first).

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__teams_list_chats
entries.description: List the Microsoft Teams chats (1:1, group, and meeting chats) the signed-in user is a member of, with each chat's id, type, topic, last-updated time, member count, and member list (group and meeting chats show at most 20 members; see memberCount for the full total). Use this to discover chat ids for teams_send_chat_message when that write-gated tool is available, or for teams:///chats/... resource reads. Results are ordered by most recent message first; note that lastUpdatedDateTime is when the chat was renamed or its membership changed, not the last-message time. The signed-in user's own notes-to-self chat typically has the id '48:notes'; if that id is not in the list, the self-chat is the oneOnOne chat whose only member is the signed-in user (use get_me to identify them). This tool lists chats only, not Teams channels. If the response includes a final item with `nextCursor`, there are more results; pass that value as the `cursor` parameter to fetch the next page. Always start with no cursor.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned in a prior response as `nextCursor`. Pass it back unchanged to fetch the next page; `limit` is ignored when `cursor` is set (the cursor carries the page size). Omit on the first call.

limit.description: Maximum number of chats to return. Default: 25, max: 25.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__teams_list_teams
entries.description: List the Microsoft Teams the signed-in user is a member of. Returns each team's id, displayName, and description. Use the id with teams_list_channels (when available) or the Teams channel tools.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__teams_reply_channel_message
entries.description: Post a reply in an existing Teams channel conversation as the signed-in user. HTML bodies are sanitized before posting. Use teams_send_channel_message to start a new conversation. Returns the created reply id and a teams:/// resource URI for the parent conversation, readable via read_resource when ChannelMessage.Read.All is granted. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

teamId.description: The id (group id GUID) of the team that owns the channel.

channelId.description: The id of the channel containing the conversation, typically of the form 19:...@thread.tacv2.

messageId.description: The id of the channel message (conversation root) to reply to, e.g. a top-level id from teams_list_channel_messages.

bodyType.description: Body content type. 'html' is sanitized against a narrow allowlist (headings, paragraphs, links, lists, basic formatting, tables, pre) before posting; tags outside the allowlist, including ,

id.description: AAD user object id (GUID) of the user to mention.

mentions.description: Users to @mention in the message. Each mention is appended to the end of the body as an <at> tag (the body is posted as HTML when mentions are supplied).

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__teams_send_channel_message

Use teams_reply_channel_message to reply in an existing conversation. Returns the created message id and a teams:/// resource URI readable via read_resource when ChannelMessage.Read.All is granted. Subject to per-user write/send rate limits — for large batches, pace operations and expect to retry after a short delay if rate-limited.

teamId.description: The id (group id GUID) of the team that owns the channel.

channelId.description: The id of the channel to post in, typically of the form 19:...@thread.tacv2.

subject.description: Optional subject line shown above the message body.

bodyType.description: Body content type. 'html' is sanitized against a narrow allowlist (headings, paragraphs, links, lists, basic formatting, tables, pre) before posting; tags outside the allowlist, including ,

id.description: AAD user object id (GUID) of the user to mention.

mentions.description: Users to @mention in the message. Each mention is appended to the end of the body as an <at> tag (the body is posted as HTML when mentions are supplied).

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__Microsoft_365__teams_send_chat_message
entries.description: Post a new message in an existing Teams chat (1:1, group, or meeting chat) as the signed-in user. The chat must already exist; this tool cannot create new chats (use teams_create_chat). HTML bodies are sanitized before posting. Returns the created message id and a teams:/// resource URI readable via read_resource when Chat.Read is granted. Group and meeting chat ids typically look like 19:...@thread.v2; 1:1 chat ids look like 19:...@unq.gbl.spaces; the signed-in user's own notes-to-self chat is typically 48:notes (if that id is absent, it is the oneOnOne chat whose only member is the signed-in user). Use teams_list_chats to discover chat ids. The chat must already exist; use teams_create_chat to create one.

bodyType.description: Body content type. 'html' is sanitized against a narrow allowlist (headings, paragraphs, links, lists, basic formatting, tables, pre) before posting; tags outside the allowlist, including ,

id.description: AAD user object id (GUID) of the user to mention.

mentions.description: Users to @mention in the message. Each mention is appended to the end of the body as an <at> tag (the body is posted as HTML when mentions are supplied).

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__project_memory_read
entries.description: Read this session's project memory. With `file` set to a bare filename (e.g. "topic.md"), returns {file, content} for that one file. Memory is a small set of markdown notes the user expects to persist across sessions in this project — read it before deciding whether earlier context applies.

entries.name: mcp__remote-devices__project_memory_write
entries.description: Write a file in this session's project memory (create or overwrite). Pass a bare `file` name ending in .md and the full `content`. To edit, call project_memory_read first and send back the whole file with your change applied. Keep MEMORY.md as a short index of one-line links to topic files; put longer notes in their own topic file. Only write what the user would want remembered across sessions.

{"method":"project_read","path":"claude/memoria-contesto.md","content":"# Monkey — memoria e contesto (per ripartire in una nuova chat)

Aggiornato al: **v1.32.0** (versionCode 56), 2026-09-02.

Questo file serve a far ripartire una nuova conversazione esattamente da dove
questa si e' fermata, senza dover rileggere l'intera cronologia della chat.
La prima parte e' un riassunto scritto a mano (progetto, regole, stato); la
seconda (appendice, in fondo) e' l'estrazione **letterale** di tutti i
commenti a blocco `/* ... */` dei sorgenti, file per file, nell'ordine in cui
compaiono — la vera memoria storica: ogni correzione porta la sua data, il
perche', e spesso la versione precedente tenuta come riferimento.

---

## 1. Cos'e' Monkey

App Android personale, senza pubblicita', per l'utente Cri: unifica la
ricerca fra **Subito.it** e **Vinted** (annunci di seconda mano). Sviluppo
un-persona, in coppia con Claude: ogni richiesta finisce con un APK firmato
+ zip dei sorgenti completi consegnati in chat.

- Package: `it.monkey.app`
- Repo locale: `/home/claude/subitoplus/` (git, branch `main`)
- Identita' git: `user.name "Monkey"`, `user.email "monkey-app@localhost"`
  — **mai** l'identita' reale dell'utente, ne' nel codice ne' nei commit.
- Consegne in: `/home/claude/out/Monkey-<versione>.apk` +
  `Monkey-<versione>-sorgenti.zip`
- Cartella Google Drive collegata (quando il bridge al dispositivo
  funziona): `G:\Il mio Drive\CRISTIANO\VIBE CODING\MONKEY\` — **nell'ultimo
  lungo tratto di lavoro il bridge non si e' mai connesso** ("device not
  connected" a ogni tentativo): si continua a tentarlo una volta per
  consegna e si ripiega senza drammi sulla sola consegna in chat.

## 2. Regole permanenti (non negoziabili, valgono sempre)

1. **Mai il nome vero o l'email dell'utente** (ne' "Cristiano"/"Zecchi" ne'
   qualunque indirizzo gmail.com) da nessuna parte nel codice, nei
   commenti, nei messaggi di commit o nell'identita' git. Prima di ogni
   consegna: `grep -rniE "cristiano|zecchi|gmail\.com"` sui sorgenti deve
   dare zero risultati.
2. **Mai `git push`** — istruzione permanente dell'utente ("non sprecare
   token a tentare il push"): il push lo fa l'utente dal proprio computer
   usando lo zip dei sorgenti consegnato.
3. **Versioning ferreo**: ogni modifica bump di `versionCode`/`versionName`
   in `app/build.gradle.kts`, con un blocco di commento datato che spiega
   il perche'. Nessuna consegna senza bump.
4. **Correzioni**: quando si cambia una sezione di codice, la versione
   precedente resta come commento datato ("--- versione precedente (fino
   alla vX.Y.Z) --- ... --- fine versione precedente ---"), non si
   cancella e basta. Le spiegazioni di "come funziona" stanno nei commenti
   dentro il codice, non solo nel messaggio di chat.
5. **Niente correzioni indovinate**: ogni fix nasce da una prova concreta
   (una sonda — cattura di traffico/JSON esportata dall'app stessa, un
   log, uno screenshot). Quando manca la prova per una feature, si spiega
   cosa servirebbe e si rimanda, invece di indovinare nomi di campo o
   forme di risposta. Esempio recente: l'icona "hai scritto al venditore"
   e' stata tolta (non lasciata sbagliata) proprio per questo — vedi §4.
6. **Manuale utente** (`Subito+ manuale.md` / equivalente rinominato) resta
   **congelato**: non aggiornarlo a meno che l'utente non lo chieda di
   nuovo esplicitamente.
7. Ogni consegna, dopo la build: verifica versione con aapt2
   (`aapt2 dump badging` → versionCode/versionName), verifica firma con
   `apksigner verify`, poi commit git (mai push), poi `SendUserFile`
   dell'APK e dello zip sorgenti, poi un tentativo di
   `device_stage_files`/`device_commit_files` verso Drive (senza insistere
   se il device non risulta connesso).
8. Attribuzione dei commit (regola di sessione, vale "da qui in avanti"):
   ogni commit termina con
   `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` e la riga
   `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01T2cLMw7XSVdUmUBdCnxwKc`
   — **verificare nella sessione corrente se questa istruzione e' stata
   rinnovata/cambiata**, potrebbe non essere piu' valida in una chat futura.

## 3. Preferenze di stile dell'utente (sempre attive)

- Risposte dirette, senza premesse introduttive.
- Quando si corregge del codice: **sempre il file/sezione intero**, mai
  solo il diff.
- Le spiegazioni di funzionamento vanno **nei commenti del codice**, non
  (solo) nel messaggio.
- Versioning tracciato e aggiornato a ogni revisione (vedi §2.3).

## 4. Architettura in breve

- **`Annuncio.kt`** — modello dati comune ai due siti (fonte, id, titolo,
  prezzo, luogo, immagine/i, descrizione, venditore, urn, preferito...).
- **`Fonti.kt`** — `FonteSubito` e `FonteVinted`: costruzione URL di
  ricerca e parsing delle risposte JSON in `List<Annuncio>`.
- **`MotoreRicerca.kt`** — motore HTTP/WebView che esegue le chiamate verso
  le due piattaforme (sessione condivisa, cookie, ecc.).
- **`StatoRicerca.kt`** — stato osservabile della schermata di ricerca:
  filtri, risultati aggregati, preferiti, nascosti, recensioni venditori.
- **`SchermataRicerca.kt`** — la UI Compose: elenco annunci (vista
  compatta/estesa), foglio filtri, home con le offerte fatte.
- **`Offerte.kt`** — le proposte di prezzo inviate dall'utente: lettura da
  Subito (`/v1/p2p/transactions`) e da Vinted (`/api/v2/inbox` +
  `/api/v2/conversations/<id>`), unificazione in un'unica mappa.
- **`LuoghiVinted.kt`** — cache luogo + numero recensioni venditore
  Vinted (`GET /api/v2/users/<id>`).
- **`RecensioniSubito.kt`** — numero recensioni venditore Subito
  (`hades.subito.it/v1/trust/feedback/public/users/...`).
- **`Controllore.kt`** — `CoroutineWorker` periodico (WorkManager) che
  controlla le ricerche salvate e notifica; guardia anti-doppio-avvio
  dalla v1.31.0.
- **`Nascosti.kt` / `Preferiti.kt` / `RicercheSalvate.kt` /
  `StoricoRicerche.kt`** — persistenza locale (file JSON in `filesDir`).
- **`MainActivity.kt`** — entry point, permessi, WorkManager, navigazione.
- **`SondaOfferte.kt` / `DomProbe.kt` / `ApiLog.kt` / `RequestLog.kt`** —
  strumenti diagnostici che l'utente lancia dal menu per catturare traffico
  reale ("sonde") quando serve una prova per un fix.

## 5. Stato attuale (fine di questo tratto di lavoro)

**v1.32.0**, versionCode 56, consegnata (APK + sorgenti) in chat; Drive non
raggiungibile, come da nota sopra.

Contenuto della v1.32.0 (le due ultime richieste dell'utente, entrambe
risolte con prove da una sonda — `bdc42069-api.json`, conversazione Vinted
con "jhnmadsu", annuncio "Rtx 3060 gaming oc 12gb - Gigabyte"):

1. **Rilanci del venditore su Vinted riconosciuti.** Prima, un'offerta mia
   rifiutata seguita da un rilancio del venditore faceva sparire l'annuncio
   dalla lista attiva: `leggiConversazioneVinted()` (in `Offerte.kt`)
   guardava solo i messaggi `offer_request_message` (le mie offerte) e
   ignorava in silenzio `offer_message` (i rilanci, un tipo distinto senza
   `status_title`). Ora i messaggi si smistano per `user_id` confrontato
   con `buyer_id`/`seller_id` della transazione, non piu' per solo tipo;
   nuovo campo `Offerta.controproposta` (centesimi del rilancio, 0 se
   nessuno); `prezzoAnnuncio` ora viene da `entity.original_price` (stabile)
   invece che da `transaction.offer_price` (che si e' scoperto diventare
   l'importo corrente/il rilancio stesso, non piu' il prezzo di listino,
   una volta che un rilancio esiste). La card "Le tue proposte"
   (`RigaOfferta` in `SchermataRicerca.kt`) mostra ora entrambe le cifre.
2. **Scorrimento foto nella vista estesa.** `Annuncio` porta ora tutte le
   foto (`immagini: List<String>`), non solo la prima; la vista estesa
   (`RigaAnnuncio`, ramo non compatto) usa un `HorizontalPager` con
   indicatore a pallini quando ce n'e' piu' di una. **Su Subito e' un dato
   certo** (stesso array `images` gia' letto in parte, solo esteso a tutti
   gli elementi). **Su Vinted e' un'estensione non ancora confermata da
   una sonda col contenuto vero**: si presume che il campo `photos`
   (plurale, visto finora solo come NOME di campo in un elenco chiavi di
   diagnostica esportata) abbia la stessa forma del gia' verificato
   `photo` (singolare, con `.url`) — se restasse vuoto o sbagliato, la
   vista ripiega da sola su una foto singola, nessun rischio di crash.
   **Prossimo passo se serve confermarlo**: una sonda API mentre si scorre
   un elenco risultati Vinted, per vedere il contenuto vero di `photos`.
   La seconda meta' della segnalazione originale dell'utente — "la
   descrizione appare solo per Subito" — **non e' un bug**: il catalogo di
   ricerca Vinted non espone quel testo (mai, non da oggi), e non c'e' modo
   di correggerlo senza una chiamata aggiuntiva per articolo (non fatta:
   nessuna richiesta esplicita dell'utente in tal senso finora).

## 6. Come procedere in una nuova chat

1. Leggere questo file per il contesto generale.
2. Se serve il dettaglio esatto di una funzione, leggere direttamente il
   sorgente in `/home/claude/subitoplus/app/src/main/java/it/monkey/app/`
   (questo file ne riassume la storia, non sostituisce il codice).
3. Verificare `git log --oneline -5` per la punta attuale del branch.
4. Rispettare sempre le regole permanenti del §2 (niente nome/email reali,
   niente push, versioning, correzioni con storico, evidenza prima di
   inventare).
5. Se l'utente riporta un problema nuovo, il riflesso e' chiedere/aspettare
   una sonda (se serve un dato che oggi non si legge) prima di scrivere
   codice che indovina la forma di una risposta.

# Monkey — memoria e contesto (per ripartire in una nuova chat)

Aggiornato al: **v1.32.0** (versionCode 56), 2026-09-02.

Questo file serve a far ripartire una nuova conversazione esattamente da dove
questa si e' fermata, senza dover rileggere l'intera cronologia della chat.
La prima parte e' un riassunto scritto a mano (progetto, regole, stato); la
seconda (appendice, in fondo) e' l'estrazione **letterale** di tutti i
commenti a blocco `/* ... */` dei sorgenti, file per file, nell'ordine in cui
compaiono — la vera memoria storica: ogni correzione porta la sua data, il
perche', e spesso la versione precedente tenuta come riferimento.

---

## 1. Cos'e' Monkey

App Android personale, senza pubblicita', per l'utente Cri: unifica la
ricerca fra **Subito.it** e **Vinted** (annunci di seconda mano). Sviluppo
un-persona, in coppia con Claude: ogni richiesta finisce con un APK firmato
+ zip dei sorgenti completi consegnati in chat.

- Package: `it.monkey.app`
- Repo locale: `/home/claude/subitoplus/` (git, branch `main`)
- Identita' git: `user.name "Monkey"`, `user.email "monkey-app@localhost"`
  — **mai** l'identita' reale dell'utente, ne' nel codice ne' nei commit.
- Consegne in: `/home/claude/out/Monkey-<versione>.apk` +
  `Monkey-<versione>-sorgenti.zip`
- Cartella Google Drive collegata (quando il bridge al dispositivo
  funziona): `G:\Il mio Drive\CRISTIANO\VIBE CODING\MONKEY\` — **nell'ultimo
  lungo tratto di lavoro il bridge non si e' mai connesso** ("device not
  connected" a ogni tentativo): si continua a tentarlo una volta per
  consegna e si ripiega senza drammi sulla sola consegna in chat.

## 2. Regole permanenti (non negoziabili, valgono sempre)

1. **Mai il nome vero o l'email dell'utente** (ne' "Cristiano"/"Zecchi" ne'
   qualunque indirizzo gmail.com) da nessuna parte nel codice, nei
   commenti, nei messaggi di commit o nell'identita' git. Prima di ogni
   consegna: `grep -rniE "cristiano|zecchi|gmail\.com"` sui sorgenti deve
   dare zero risultati.
2. **Mai `git push`** — istruzione permanente dell'utente ("non sprecare
   token a tentare il push"): il push lo fa l'utente dal proprio computer
   usando lo zip dei sorgenti consegnato.
3. **Versioning ferreo**: ogni modifica bump di `versionCode`/`versionName`
   in `app/build.gradle.kts`, con un blocco di commento datato che spiega
   il perche'. Nessuna consegna senza bump.
4. **Correzioni**: quando si cambia una sezione di codice, la versione
   precedente resta come commento datato ("--- versione precedente (fino
   alla vX.Y.Z) --- ... --- fine versione precedente ---"), non si
   cancella e basta. Le spiegazioni di "come funziona" stanno nei commenti
   dentro il codice, non solo nel messaggio di chat.
5. **Niente correzioni indovinate**: ogni fix nasce da una prova concreta
   (una sonda — cattura di traffico/JSON esportata dall'app stessa, un
   log, uno screenshot). Quando manca la prova per una feature, si spiega
   cosa servirebbe e si rimanda, invece di indovinare nomi di campo o
   forme di risposta. Esempio recente: l'icona "hai scritto al venditore"
   e' stata tolta (non lasciata sbagliata) proprio per questo — vedi §4.
6. **Manuale utente** (`Subito+ manuale.md` / equivalente rinominato) resta
   **congelato**: non aggiornarlo a meno che l'utente non lo chieda di
   nuovo esplicitamente.
7. Ogni consegna, dopo la build: verifica versione con aapt2
   (`aapt2 dump badging` → versionCode/versionName), verifica firma con
   `apksigner verify`, poi commit git (mai push), poi `SendUserFile`
   dell'APK e dello zip sorgenti, poi un tentativo di
   `device_stage_files`/`device_commit_files` verso Drive (senza insistere
   se il device non risulta connesso).
8. Attribuzione dei commit (regola di sessione, vale "da qui in avanti"):
   ogni commit termina con
   `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` e la riga
   `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01T2cLMw7XSVdUmUBdCnxwKc`
   — **verificare nella sessione corrente se questa istruzione e' stata
   rinnovata/cambiata**, potrebbe non essere piu' valida in una chat futura.

## 3. Preferenze di stile dell'utente (sempre attive)

- Risposte dirette, senza premesse introduttive.
- Quando si corregge del codice: **sempre il file/sezione intero**, mai
  solo il diff.
- Le spiegazioni di funzionamento vanno **nei commenti del codice**, non
  (solo) nel messaggio.
- Versioning tracciato e aggiornato a ogni revisione (vedi §2.3).

## 4. Architettura in breve

- **`Annuncio.kt`** — modello dati comune ai due siti (fonte, id, titolo,
  prezzo, luogo, immagine/i, descrizione, venditore, urn, preferito...).
- **`Fonti.kt`** — `FonteSubito` e `FonteVinted`: costruzione URL di
  ricerca e parsing delle risposte JSON in `List<Annuncio>`.
- **`MotoreRicerca.kt`** — motore HTTP/WebView che esegue le chiamate verso
  le due piattaforme (sessione condivisa, cookie, ecc.).
- **`StatoRicerca.kt`** — stato osservabile della schermata di ricerca:
  filtri, risultati aggregati, preferiti, nascosti, recensioni venditori.
- **`SchermataRicerca.kt`** — la UI Compose: elenco annunci (vista
  compatta/estesa), foglio filtri, home con le offerte fatte.
- **`Offerte.kt`** — le proposte di prezzo inviate dall'utente: lettura da
  Subito (`/v1/p2p/transactions`) e da Vinted (`/api/v2/inbox` +
  `/api/v2/conversations/<id>`), unificazione in un'unica mappa.
- **`LuoghiVinted.kt`** — cache luogo + numero recensioni venditore
  Vinted (`GET /api/v2/users/<id>`).
- **`RecensioniSubito.kt`** — numero recensioni venditore Subito
  (`hades.subito.it/v1/trust/feedback/public/users/...`).
- **`Controllore.kt`** — `CoroutineWorker` periodico (WorkManager) che
  controlla le ricerche salvate e notifica; guardia anti-doppio-avvio
  dalla v1.31.0.
- **`Nascosti.kt` / `Preferiti.kt` / `RicercheSalvate.kt` /
  `StoricoRicerche.kt`** — persistenza locale (file JSON in `filesDir`).
- **`MainActivity.kt`** — entry point, permessi, WorkManager, navigazione.
- **`SondaOfferte.kt` / `DomProbe.kt` / `ApiLog.kt` / `RequestLog.kt`** —
  strumenti diagnostici che l'utente lancia dal menu per catturare traffico
  reale ("sonde") quando serve una prova per un fix.

## 5. Stato attuale (fine di questo tratto di lavoro)

**v1.32.0**, versionCode 56, consegnata (APK + sorgenti) in chat; Drive non
raggiungibile, come da nota sopra.

Contenuto della v1.32.0 (le due ultime richieste dell'utente, entrambe
risolte con prove da una sonda — `bdc42069-api.json`, conversazione Vinted
con "jhnmadsu", annuncio "Rtx 3060 gaming oc 12gb - Gigabyte"):

1. **Rilanci del venditore su Vinted riconosciuti.** Prima, un'offerta mia
   rifiutata seguita da un rilancio del venditore faceva sparire l'annuncio
   dalla lista attiva: `leggiConversazioneVinted()` (in `Offerte.kt`)
   guardava solo i messaggi `offer_request_message` (le mie offerte) e
   ignorava in silenzio `offer_message` (i rilanci, un tipo distinto senza
   `status_title`). Ora i messaggi si smistano per `user_id` confrontato
   con `buyer_id`/`seller_id` della transazione, non piu' per solo tipo;
   nuovo campo `Offerta.controproposta` (centesimi del rilancio, 0 se
   nessuno); `prezzoAnnuncio` ora viene da `entity.original_price` (stabile)
   invece che da `transaction.offer_price` (che si e' scoperto diventare
   l'importo corrente/il rilancio stesso, non piu' il prezzo di listino,
   una volta che un rilancio esiste). La card "Le tue proposte"
   (`RigaOfferta` in `SchermataRicerca.kt`) mostra ora entrambe le cifre.
2. **Scorrimento foto nella vista estesa.** `Annuncio` porta ora tutte le
   foto (`immagini: List<String>`), non solo la prima; la vista estesa
   (`RigaAnnuncio`, ramo non compatto) usa un `HorizontalPager` con
   indicatore a pallini quando ce n'e' piu' di una. **Su Subito e' un dato
   certo** (stesso array `images` gia' letto in parte, solo esteso a tutti
   gli elementi). **Su Vinted e' un'estensione non ancora confermata da
   una sonda col contenuto vero**: si presume che il campo `photos`
   (plurale, visto finora solo come NOME di campo in un elenco chiavi di
   diagnostica esportata) abbia la stessa forma del gia' verificato
   `photo` (singolare, con `.url`) — se restasse vuoto o sbagliato, la
   vista ripiega da sola su una foto singola, nessun rischio di crash.
   **Prossimo passo se serve confermarlo**: una sonda API mentre si scorre
   un elenco risultati Vinted, per vedere il contenuto vero di `photos`.
   La seconda meta' della segnalazione originale dell'utente — "la
   descrizione appare solo per Subito" — **non e' un bug**: il catalogo di
   ricerca Vinted non espone quel testo (mai, non da oggi), e non c'e' modo
   di correggerlo senza una chiamata aggiuntiva per articolo (non fatta:
   nessuna richiesta esplicita dell'utente in tal senso finora).

### Cose aperte / in sospeso

- **Feedback non ancora arrivato**: se il fix del rilancio Vinted e lo
  scorrimento foto funzionano davvero sul campo (specialmente il caso
  Vinted `photos[]`, inferenza non confermata).
- **Guardia anti-doppio-avvio (v1.31.0)**: aggiunta ma non ancora
  confermata dall'utente come risolutiva (serviva un nuovo
  `controllo-log.txt` pulito per dirlo con certezza).
- **Icona "hai scritto al venditore"** (v1.28.0, poi tolta in v1.31.0):
  in pausa. Serve una sonda che catturi (a) una conversazione Vinted
  **senza** offerta (per vedere la sua forma JSON) e (b) un endpoint
  Subito che elenchi le conversazioni chat in generale (oggi si vede solo
  il conteggio non letti e le transazioni P2P). Quando arrivano: icona a
  forma di busta (`Icons.Filled.Email`), mostrata SOLO per messaggi senza
  offerta di prezzo (se c'e' un'offerta, il testo con l'importo basta gia').
- **Filtro "scarta venditori senza recensioni"**: attivo su entrambe le
  fonti dalla v1.30.0, nessun problema noto.

## 6. Come procedere in una nuova chat

1. Leggere questo file per il contesto generale.
2. Se serve il dettaglio esatto di una funzione, leggere direttamente il
   sorgente in `/home/claude/subitoplus/app/src/main/java/it/monkey/app/`
   (questo file ne riassume la storia, non sostituisce il codice).
3. Verificare `git log --oneline -5` per la punta attuale del branch.
4. Rispettare sempre le regole permanenti del §2 (niente nome/email reali,
   niente push, versioning, correzioni con storico, evidenza prima di
   inventare).
5. Se l'utente riporta un problema nuovo, il riflesso e' chiedere/aspettare
   una sonda (se serve un dato che oggi non si legge) prima di scrivere
   codice che indovina la forma di una risposta.
